title: Uno Platform 7.0 Adds WebGPU Backend, Apple TV and Reactor Support, and Retires Native Rendering
gist: Uno Platform 7.0 consolidates all targets on SkiaSharp 4 with an experimental WebGPU backend, extends .NET MAUI third-party controls and Microsoft.UI.Reactor to every platform, adds Apple TV and .NET 11, and retires native rendering and Mac Catalyst with binary-breaking changes.

insights.claim: Uno Platform 7.0 unifies rendering for all targets on a single pluggable pipeline with SkiaSharp 4 as default, Vulkan by default on Android, Windows and Linux, and an experimental WebGPU backend across desktop, mobile and WebAssembly.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Cross-platform .NET UI is consolidating on GPU-drawn rendering rather than native controls, mirroring Flutter-style approaches.
insights.locator: All targets now render through one pluggable pipeline

insights.claim: Uno Platform reports 7.0 is about 2x faster at the median and 5x smaller than 6.7, with brush creation up to 38x faster, but these are vendor benchmarks with unpublished workloads.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Treat performance claims cautiously until independently reproduced.
insights.locator: Uno Platform is an open-source framework

insights.claim: Uno Platform's WebGPU backend delivered up to 50% frame-rate improvement depending on scene and lets a WebGPU-only app drop about 6 MB of uncompressed native code from WebAssembly builds.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: WebGPU is maturing into a practical production rendering target for app frameworks.
insights.locator: The WebGPU backend, available on all desktop

insights.claim: Uno Platform is co-maintainer of the SkiaSharp library alongside Microsoft's .NET team.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Signals deepening ties between Uno and Microsoft's .NET ecosystem.

insights.claim: Through .NET MAUI Embedding, third-party controls from Syncfusion, Telerik, Infragistics, DevExpress and Esri now run on every Uno Platform target including web and Linux, and existing .NET MAUI apps can reach browser and Linux via Uno's MAUI handlers.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Uno is positioning as the path to extend .NET MAUI investments to web and Linux, expanding addressable market for .NET control vendors.

insights.claim: Microsoft.UI.Reactor, Microsoft's declarative XAML-free C# framework for WinUI with hooks like UseState, now runs in preview on Uno's desktop, browser, Android and iOS targets and can coexist with XAML pages.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Microsoft's .NET UI direction is shifting toward React-style declarative C#, with Uno as a cross-platform carrier.

insights.claim: Uno Platform 7.0 adds Apple TV via net10.0-tvos (tvOS 15+, Metal rendering, Siri Remote focus) and supports .NET 11 from day zero, while .NET 10 remains the long-term support option.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Continued target expansion (after Android TV, Android Auto, Wear OS in 6.7) broadens Uno's device coverage.

insights.claim: Uno Platform 7.0 retires native rendering and removes Mac Catalyst, makes Uno.Sdk single-project the only supported format, and makes libraries built against 6.x binary-incompatible, requiring rebuilds.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Upgrade friction for the Uno ecosystem; third-party library vendors must ship rebuilt packages.

insights.claim: Uno Platform 7.0 is described by the team as its largest release, with 5,219 commits and 704 closed issues since 6.7, following 6.7 in September which removed WPF targets.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Rapid release cadence indicates an actively invested open-source .NET UI project.
insights.locator: The team describes 7.0 as its largest release
